hypothesis: Frozen ImageNet-derived features may limit material and foreground adaptation. Fine-tuning only the final three encoder blocks could improve held-out whole-heart predictions while preserving early features. It may overfit the small real corpus.
protocol: Both arms start from the identical retained synthetic foreground checkpoint, with the same neutral material head, seed, 240 updates, four-image batches, print/reflection/synthetic schedules, nineteen reviewed photos, and two connected source/motif folds.
One serial CPU thread. No evaluation image or label can enter its own training fold. The synthetic-only control is also retained for both arms.
The only learning-policy change is allowing blocks 9, 10 and 11 to update at 0.0001 while all other trainable parameters keep 0.001. BatchNorm buffers remain frozen everywhere.
Use the fixed final update, without early stopping, checkpoint selection, held-out tuning or topology-based candidate selection.
Independently audit initial/frozen tensors, group exclusion, draw schedule, checkpoint inference and reported metrics. Compare on identical partial observations.

If material/body metrics or crops show a gain, test the full photo-to-editable-template pipeline and visually inspect changes before claiming useful reconstruction. New lower-error masks alone are insufficient.
limitations: Repeatedly inspected development photos, nineteen images and two broad source/motif groups; not an unseen test.
One seed and fixed 240-update budget; a negative outcome does not rule out other adaptation policies.
Encoder parameter updates can change semantics even though BatchNorm statistics remain frozen.
No production integration, ONNX deployment, pushing or changes to physical/template acceptance thresholds.
